note: Study skeleton paraphrased from the course scope (not verbatim College Board prose; unit numbers are our own sequencing, not official CED numbers). Skill codes are indicative: 1.x concept, 2.x/3.x skill.

objectives.statement: Explain how democracies and authoritarian regimes differ in legitimacy, participation, and power.
Classify regimes using institutional and behavioral evidence.

units.title: UK, Russia, China, Iran, Nigeria, Mexico: Institutions

topics.title: UK, Russia, China, Iran, Nigeria, Mexico: Institutions

objectives.statement: Explain how the six core countries organize constitutions, executives, legislatures, and judiciaries.
Compare executive-legislative relations across parliamentary, presidential, and hybrid systems.
Explain how party systems and electoral rules shape representation in the six countries.
Predict how electoral-system changes would alter party competition.
Explain how history, religion, and ethnicity shape political culture and participation.
Analyze survey and demographic evidence about legitimacy and trust.
Explain democratization, revolution, and market transitions in comparative cases.
Evaluate why similar shocks produce different regime outcomes.
Explain how trade, migration, and international organizations constrain and empower states.
Analyze a global issue through the institutions of two core countries.
